prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: low-speed head-on collision in Katy, Texas. Injury: concussion. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1023; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather not give my full name on the record. You can refer to me as the plaintiff.

Q: That's fine for today. Let's start with the accident. Where were you on the day of the collision?

A: I was driving north on a two-lane road in Katy, Texas, heading to the grocery store near my house. It was mid-morning and the road was dry.

Q: What were you doing right before the impact?

A: I had slowed down because traffic ahead was backing up. I was stopped, or nearly stopped, when the other car crossed into my lane.

Q: Do you know how fast the other vehicle was moving?

A: Not exactly. It didn't look like it was going very fast. It was more of a jolt than a crash. Both cars were pretty banged up in the front, but nothing like the highway wrecks you see on the news.

Q: Did you hit your head?

A: I think my head snapped forward and then back against the headrest. I remember hitting something, maybe the steering wheel or the window frame. It happened fast.

Q: What did you do immediately afterward?

A: I sat there for a minute trying to figure out what happened. Someone came over and asked if I was okay. I said yes, because I didn't want to make a fuss. Looking back, I wasn't really thinking clearly.

Q: When did you first notice symptoms?

A: That evening. I had a headache that got worse, and the lights in the kitchen seemed too bright. I also felt foggy, like I was walking through water.

Q: Did you seek medical treatment?

A: I went to an urgent care clinic the next morning. They sent me for a scan and then referred me to a neurologist. I've been seeing her every few weeks since then.

Q: Since the accident, how has your daily routine changed?

A: I used to work full days and go to the gym most evenings. Now I need breaks from screens, and I can't work more than a few hours before I get a pounding headache. I've had to ask my manager for a reduced schedule. I also stopped driving at night because the glare bothers me.

Q: Has anyone helped you with household tasks?

A: My sister comes over on weekends to help with cooking and laundry. Some days I just lie in a dark room and wait for the symptoms to pass.
